assignmentIntro: Plan the assignment at your own pace: every change stays a draft until you apply it in the finish tab. Participants only see the result once the assignment is released.
assignmentIntroApplyText: In the Finish tab you write the draft into the registrations: delegations are split and merged, roles handed out. Ratings and weighting are kept.
assignmentIntroDelegationsText: Hand out nations and non-state actors to delegations – by drag and drop or automatically for all open groups of one size. The automatic assignment only uses roles with exactly as many free seats as the group has members. If a delegation does not fit, split it into parts; two small delegations can be merged this way as well.
assignmentIntroDraftText: Everything you plan stays a draft on top of the real registrations. It can be discarded at any time and changes nothing.
assignmentIntroFinishText: Check what the planned changes do, resolve problems that block applying and apply the assignment. The switch to release it is here as well.
assignmentIntroLead: The assignment runs through the tabs in five steps, from left to right. You can switch between them at any time and work in any order – none of it is visible to participants until you apply and release it.

A red warning next to a name points to a global note about earlier behavior. The arrow keys switch the application, N jumps to the next one nobody has looked at. Everything is saved for the whole team right away.

conferenceStatusDescription:
The conference status determines what participants can see and do in the app. It should only ever be changed "forward". Even though no data is lost when taking a step back, it can lead to confusion among participants and potentially cause unexpected behavior in the app.

The conference status is oriented around the phases of a conference. The possibilities are:

  • Before registration starts: The conference has been created, but the registration phase has not yet started. All preparations can be made, but registration is not yet possible, and the conference is not yet visible externally.
  • Registration Phase: Registration is possible until the end date for registration is reached. Then the registration phase is automatically ended. Now allocation can be made and also already applied. As long as the conference status is still "Registration Phase", participants cannot yet see their assignment.
  • Preparation Phase: When the allocation is complete and you want to announce the results, the conference status can be set to "Preparation Phase".This status should remain until the beginning of the conference.Participants will be shown information about postal registration and contribution payment and can access materials and information.
  • Active Conference: This status should be set shortly before the start of the conference.
  • After the Conference: After the conference, the status can be set to "After the Conference". Before this, it should be recorded who among the participants was present and should receive a certificate. With this status, participants can download their certificates.

homeAboutUsText: DMUN is a non-profit organization of young adults who are passionate about international politics and the United Nations. We are active nationwide and internationally in the field of political youth education and youth empowerment. Founded in 2003 and accredited as a non-governmental organization with special consultative status with the United Nations Economic and Social Council and UNDPI since 2012, we organize political simulation games in which teenagers and young adults between the ages of 15 and 21 simulate a United Nations conference. We also promote political youth education and the participation of young people in political processes at an international level.

postalRegistrationFAQ1:
Where should I send my documents?

Please send your documents, thoroughly completed and signed (by you and your parents if applicable), to the following address:
postalRegistrationFAQ2: Please ensure that you have sufficient postage, especially for shipments from abroad.
postalRegistrationInstructions:
In order to participate in the conference, we need a few signed documents from you by postal mail – meaning the original copies sent by letter (no photocopies). We provide the documents as a package in a PDF for download. The following documents are included:

  • the binding registration, which is based on our terms of use and privacy policy and which you must sign yourself
  • the declaration of consent from all parents or guardians, which normally must be signed by both (!) parents if you are not of legal age by the start of the conference ({conferenceStart})
  • the declaration of consent for image use, which must be signed by you and – if you are not of legal age at the time of the conference – additionally by all of your parents or guardians

You must print them (you can choose to not print the terms and conditions at the end of the document to save paper), fill in all the required fields, and then sign them as described above, and also have your parents sign them if necessary.

Our Terms and Conditions should be read, but do not need to be printed.

Unfortunately, it is not sufficient to simply sign the postal registration electronically or send it to us by scan. We, too, would much prefer to avoid the hassle of paperwork. Unfortunately, the legal framework in Germany does not allow this. Therefore, there is no way around sending the documents by post.

resolutionImportLLMPromptPreamble:
Format the following UN resolution preamble clauses. Each clause must:
- Start with an italicized opening phrase (e.g., Recognizing, Noting with concern, Recalling)
- Be on its own line
- Not include any numbering
- Trailing punctuation (commas, semicolons) is optional and will be handled automatically

Example format:
Recognizing the importance of international cooperation
Noting with concern the ongoing challenges

Here is my text to format:
resolutionImportTipsOperative2: Sub-clause hierarchy: I., II. (first level) → a), b) (second) → aa), bb) (third)
resolutionImportTipsOperative3: End clauses with semicolons (;) and the final clause with a period (.)
resolutionImportTipsOperative4: Indentation helps but is not required - the parser detects structure from numbering
resolutionImportTipsPreamble1: Each preamble clause should start with an italicized opening phrase (e.g., "Recognizing", "Noting with concern")
